title: Code beside its chart

steps.say: With echo: true the code goes on the slide, and the chart under it runs off the bottom. Code and chart fight for the same space.
output-location: column puts the code on the left and the chart on the right. Both fit, and the eye goes from one to the other.
column-fragment holds the chart back. Explain the code first; the room cannot read ahead.
One click, and the result appears beside the code that made it.

---
title: "Unemployment in the regions"
subtitle: "Quarterly briefing · synthetic data"
format:
  revealjs:
    chalkboard: true
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
kingdom <- rates |> filter(region == "Kingdom")
jazan <- rates |> filter(region == "Jazan")
change <- rates |>
  filter(region != "Kingdom") |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(change = last(rate) - first(rate))
up <- change |> filter(change > 0) |> pull(region)
```

## Unemployment is falling

::: {.incremental}
- Down in `r sum(change$change < 0)` of `r nrow(change)` regions since 2022
- It rose only in `r up`
:::

::: {.notes}
Pause here. Ask the room which region surprised them.
:::

. . .

Next: why Jazan is different.

## The national trend

```{r}
ggplot(kingdom, aes(date, rate)) + geom_line()
```

# How the chart is made

## Reading the pipeline

```{r}

#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "|1|2|3-4"
rates |>
  filter(region == "Jazan") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, rate)) +
  geom_line()
```
